content:
incident-bot: ALERT: dedicated-eu-2 pool GPU saturation >95% for 6m, 99p latency spike. Triggered by surge in text-generation embeddings. Incident ticket: INC-2026-487. Metrics: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/dedicated-eu-2

alex_chan (oncall): grabbing it. seeing 503s in the proxy logs too. initial triage: autoscaler didn't add replicas for last 10m.

maya_ng (sre): can you paste the autoscaler logs? wondering if spot preemption or scaling cooldowns kicked in. also check burst_capacity config on the pool.

alex_chan (oncall): logs attached (snippet):
```
[2026-03-15T18:02:12Z] autoscaler: evaluate pool dedicated-eu-2 current_replicas=4 desired=4 cooldown_remaining=0s
[2026-03-15T18:03:12Z] autoscaler: scale_evaluation:_cpu 97% -> no_change (policy: respect_max_replicas)
[2026-03-15T18:04:10Z] rpc: failed to provision new node: quota_exceeded for eu region
```
looks like quota_exceeded prevented scale out.

sophie_kim (platform): ah — that's the reserved capacity soft cap. we have burst_capacity=2 configured for that pool. we can bump burst to handle short surges. will need a manual toggle + approval.

alex_chan (oncall): proposed immediate mitigations (short list):
- toggle burst_capacity from 2 -> 6 on dedicated-eu-2
- temporarily lower autoscaler min_replicas to allow faster scale semantics? (or increase max_replicas)
- apply per-plan rate limit for non-enterprise customers to shed load
- disable experimental rerank-v2 on Dedicated (it spikes memory usage)

maya_ng (sre): +1. prioritize burst toggle + rate limiting. rerank-v2 disable if still degraded after the first two.

alex_chan (oncall): performing burst toggle now. command to platform admin:
```bash
# adminctl is internal tool for pool changes
adminctl pools update dedicated-eu-2 --set burst_capacity=6 --reason "oncall: surge mitigation"
```
executing...

deploy-bot: ACTION REQUIRED: increase burst_capacity requires 2 approvals. Approvers: @sophie_kim, @maya_ng. Use `/approve ACTION_ID` to approve. ACTION_ID=act-6729

sophie_kim (platform): approved. /approve act-6729 :white_check_mark:

maya_ng (sre): approved. /approve act-6729 :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: ACTION LOG: act-6729 approved by 2 users. Applying change...

deploy-bot: CHANGE SUCCESS: burst_capacity for dedicated-eu-2 set to 6. Change id: change-9881

alex_chan (oncall): now applying route-level soft rate limit for non-enterprise customers to 20r/s per api-key. small JSON rule pasted below and pushed to traffic-shaper service:
```json
{
  "scope": "dedicated-eu-2",
  "match": "plan != \"enterprise\"",
  "limit": "20r/s",
  "action": "queue_or_429",
  "duration": "10m",
  "reason": "temp surge mitigation 2026-03-15"
}
```

liam_support: we've got customer tickets relating to 503s: CUST-3412 (fin-tech) and CUST-3420 (analytics). both on standard plan. I pinged their CS reps and asked for patience. they saw failures starting ~18:01 UTC.

maya_ng (sre): monitoring tail latency and 5xx rate now. grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/pool-dedicated-eu-2?from=now-20m&to=now

maya_ng (sre): early signs: 99p latency dropped from 2.1s -> 0.9s after burst toggle + rate-limit. 5xx rate down from 2.3% -> 0.4%. still watching.

alex_chan (oncall): still seeing some memory pressure on a subset of workers attributed to rerank-v2 model. proprosal: disable rerank-v2 on dedicated pools for the next 30m. Sophie can flip the feature flag.

sophie_kim (platform): will flip it. commiting temporary feature-flag change:
```bash
# ffctl toggles feature flags in config-service
ffctl set rerank-v2 --scope dedicated --enabled false --expires "2026-03-15T19:00:00Z" --reason "Autoscale surge mitigation"
```
ffctl: change queued, awaiting rollout to config-service nodes...

deploy-bot: FeatureFlag: rerank-v2 scope=dedicated disabled by sophie_kim. rollout-id=ff-4412

alex_chan (oncall): good, monitoring again. metrics look better. linking recent proxy logs showing reduced 503s:
```
[18:10:02Z] proxy: 200 ok tokens=345 latency=120ms
[18:10:02Z] proxy: 504 gateway timeout client=10.2.3.44 route=generate (down from 5/min)
```

maya_ng (sre): quick note — we still need to follow up on quota_exceeded that blocked autoscaler earlier. ops needs to request region quota bump or pre-allocate standby capacity.

alex_chan (oncall): agree. created ops ticket OPS-1278 to request long-term quota change for eu region. linking: https://tickets.redwood.internal/OPS-1278

liam_support: customer updates: told CUST-3412 and CUST-3420 we applied temporary rate limits and increased pool burst to reduce errors. both asked for ETA on full resolution. said we'll follow up in postmortem.

maya_ng (sre): summary so far (for handoff):
- root cause: sudden traffic surge + region quota_exceeded prevented autoscaler scale-out -> pool saturated
- short-term mitigation: increased burst_capacity 2->6, applied per-plan rate limiting (20r/s non-enterprise), disabled rerank-v2 feature for dedicated pools
- status: 5xx and 99p latency back to acceptable ranges; ongoing monitoring for 30m
- next actions: ops to request quota bump (OPS-1278), platform to propose autoscaler policy change to prefer faster scale-out under high GPU util, consider pre-warming standby nodes

alex_chan (oncall): handing off to @maya_ng for monitoring and next steps. I'm stepping off at 19:30 UTC. key artifacts: change-9881 (burst toggle), ff-4412 (feature flag), adminctl logs (attached).

maya_ng (sre): ack. I'll take it and keep eyes for 1h. setting watch: monitor-alerts @channel for next 60m.

sophie_kim (platform): follow-up: I'll propose new pool policy in PR later today — increase burst default for EU pools and add automated quota-check preflight before scale attempts.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity degraded to SEV3 (degraded performance). 5xx rate within baseline. Incident will remain open for monitoring.

maya_ng (sre): decision note: we should also tune autoscaler max_replicas up for this pool to avoid hitting quota_exceeded logic; will draft a plan and post in #eng-runtime.

alex_chan (oncall): thanks everyone. leaving handoff notes in OPS ticket and will summarize in postmortems channel once incident closed. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: metrics stable for 20m, errors at baseline. Closing incident INC-2026-487 and creating postmortem draft: https://pm.redwood.internal/INC-2026-487-pm

maya_ng (sre): moving to postmortem stage. I'll collect logs and timeline tomorrow.

liam_support: closing customer tickets with summary + apology. will attach postmortem link when ready.

sophie_kim (platform): +1 on postmortem. will include change-9881 and ff-4412 in the timeline.

deploy-bot: INCIDENT LOGGED: INC-2026-487 closed by incident-bot at 2026-03-15T19:02:00Z.
